project_reference.core_research_question: Reactor-CEvNS, cosmic-muon, and environmental-gamma Compton spectra in reconstructed energy for a 4"×4"×2mm single-sided Ge wafer read out by QPDs (Ta→Al and Al→Hf designs).

scope.question: What are the reactor-CEvNS, cosmic-ray-muon, and environmental-gamma Compton differential rate spectra in reconstructed energy for a 4 inch x 4 inch x 2 mm single-sided Ge wafer read out by QPDs with Ta->Al and Al->Hf trapping designs?
in_scope: Reactor CEvNS differential rate spectrum in reconstructed energy for a 3 GWth commercial reactor at 25 m standoff with a 4-isotope Huber-Mueller-like antineutrino spectrum plus an explicit sub-1.8 MeV treatment

Cosmic-ray muon energy-deposit spectrum in reconstructed energy for the thin wafer, including chord-length geometry (short vertical crossings and long near-horizontal chords) and Landau-Vavilov straggling
Compton-scattering electron-recoil spectrum in reconstructed energy from a representative environmental radiogenic gamma background (U/Th chains plus K-40 lines and continuum) in the thin wafer

Detector response model: deposited energy to ~50% signal efficiency, trapped quasiparticle number, EMG-profiled tunneling burst, 50 kHz bandwidth-limited reconstruction with perfect tunneling identification
Both trapping designs: Ta absorber to Al trap/junction and Al absorber to Hf trap/junction
Detector geometry: 4 inch x 4 inch x 2 mm Ge wafer (about 110 g), single instrumented face with QPD sensor density of 1 per mm^2 (about 10300 sensors)
out_of_scope: G4CMP phonon-transport simulation (deferred to a later stage)
Imperfect quasiparticle-tunneling identification and readout-noise modeling
Neutron-induced nuclear-recoil backgrounds and other backgrounds beyond cosmic-ray muons and environmental-gamma Compton scattering
unresolved_questions: How should reconstruction behave in the saturated regime: simple Nyquist rate-clip or a dead-time model (paralyzable vs non-paralyzable)?
How should the Ta->Al device tunneling parameters be mapped from the QPD paper's tabulated Al- and Hf-junction devices?
What absolute environmental gamma flux and line composition best represent a surface-level reactor-site deployment?

known_good_baselines: J. Billard et al., J. Phys. G 44, 105101 (2017), arXiv:1612.09035 (Ge CEvNS reactor rate predictions, Table 1: 0.76/0.51/0.26 counts/kg/day above 50/100/200 eV_nr)
CONUS+ Collaboration, Nature 643, 1229 (2025), arXiv:2501.05206 (observed reactor CEvNS on Ge at 3.6 GWth, 20.7 m)
context_gaps: Ta->Al device tunneling parameters (K, Gamma_out, tau_qp) not tabulated in the QPD paper
Absolute environmental gamma flux normalization for the Compton channel not yet fixed
crucial_inputs: 100% phonon collection with ~50% overall deposited-energy-to-signal efficiency
50 kHz signal bandwidth: tunneling faster than the ~25 kHz Nyquist rate is unresolvable
Perfect identification of quasiparticle tunneling events
4 inch x 4 inch x 2 mm single-sided Ge wafer, about 110 g
QPD sensor density of 1 per mm^2 on one face, about 10300 sensors
Commercial 3 GWth reactor at 25 m standoff
Sea-level muon flux with no overburden
Representative environmental radiogenic gamma background for the Compton channel
Exponentially-modified-Gaussian pulse template from the qpd repo
Unified phonon energy scale with no ionization quenching for nuclear and electron recoils

formulations: Freedman CEvNS differential cross section with Helm form factor on natural Ge folded with a 4-isotope reactor antineutrino spectrum
Klein-Nishina Compton scattering of a representative environmental gamma spectrum, thin-target single-scatter dominated, on Ge
Analytic and Monte-Carlo response chain from deposited energy to bandwidth-limited reconstructed energy using the QPD paper pulse model and the qpd-repo EMG template
allowed_estimator_families: Direct spectrum folding and Monte-Carlo sampling of the response chain
allowed_fit_families: EMG pulse-template fits for energy reconstruction
stop_and_rethink_conditions: The CEvNS reconstructed spectrum falls entirely below the effective threshold for both designs
Muon-induced or gamma-induced pileup at sea level makes quiescent reconstruction impossible at 50 kHz bandwidth

observables.name: Environmental-gamma Compton spectrum

claims.statement: The reactor CEvNS spectrum in reconstructed energy is computed for both trapping designs and its total rate agrees with published Ge reactor predictions within a factor of about 2

The sea-level muon spectrum in reconstructed energy is computed for both designs with the chord-length geometry and bandwidth-saturation regime made explicit, and the integral muon rate matches the PDG sea-level flux through the wafer

The Compton electron-recoil spectrum from a representative environmental radiogenic gamma background is computed in reconstructed energy for the wafer, showing Compton continua and edges on the unified phonon energy scale
The reconstructed-versus-deposited energy response, including saturation from the 25 kHz maximum resolvable tunneling rate, is derived for both trapping designs

deliverables.description: CEvNS, muon, and Compton differential rate spectra versus reconstructed energy for both trapping designs
must_contain: all three channels: CEvNS, muon, Compton

deliverables.description: Reconstructed versus deposited energy response with the saturation onset marked
Python implementation of the CEvNS, muon, and Compton spectrum calculations and the QPD response pipeline
must_contain: response chain from deposited to reconstructed energy

deliverables.description: Assumptions and results note for the stage-1 rough estimate

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-cevns
acceptance_tests.procedure: Reproduce Billard et al. (2017) Table 1 Ge rates under their assumptions, then rescale to 3 GWth at 25 m and compare
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Billard Table 1 reproduced within about 20 percent and rescaled rate consistent within a factor of 2

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-muon
acceptance_tests.procedure: Integrate the muon event rate through the wafer and compare with the PDG sea-level flux times the wafer geometric acceptance

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-compton
acceptance_tests.procedure: Check that Compton edges appear at the Klein-Nishina energies E_edge = 2 E_gamma^2 / (m_e c^2 + 2 E_gamma) for the assumed gamma lines and that the total interaction rate matches the assumed flux times the Ge Compton cross section over the wafer
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Compton edges at predicted energies and interaction rate within a factor of about 2 of the flux-times-cross-section estimate

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-response
acceptance_tests.procedure: Check the low-energy limit (reconstructed energy equals 0.5 times deposited energy within statistical scatter) and the high-energy limit (response saturates once the tunneling rate exceeds 25 kHz)
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Both limiting behaviors reproduced by the pipeline

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-cevns
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Reporting spectra in deposited energy only without the reconstruction and bandwidth model
forbidden_proxies.reason: The decisive output is the spectrum in reconstructed energy

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-muon
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Muon spectrum computed without the 50 kHz bandwidth saturation model or without chord-length geometry
forbidden_proxies.reason: Saturation and thin-wafer geometry shape the muon response and omitting them would look like progress while skipping the decisive physics

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-compton
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Treating gamma deposits as full-energy photopeaks instead of the Compton continuum expected in a thin 2 mm wafer
forbidden_proxies.reason: In a thin wafer gammas predominantly single-Compton-scatter and escape, so the continuum, not photopeaks, is the physical signal

weakest_anchors: The lumped ~50% deposited-to-signal efficiency replaces the paper's design-dependent efficiency chain
Ta->Al device tunneling parameters are extrapolated rather than tabulated in the QPD paper
The absolute environmental gamma flux normalization for the Compton channel is a representative assumption, not a site measurement
unvalidated_assumptions: Uniform phonon-energy sharing among the ~10300 QPD sensors on the single instrumented face
qpd-repo EMG template parameters apply to a Ge wafer
Thin-wafer single-Compton-scatter dominance for the gamma background
disconfirming_observations: Computed total CEvNS rate disagrees with published Ge reactor predictions by more than an order of magnitude
The response chain shows no saturation even when tunneling rates far exceed the 25 kHz Nyquist limit
Compton edges appear at energies inconsistent with the Klein-Nishina prediction

decisions.summary: Design->parameter mapping locked in code: Ta->Al uses Table II Aluminum column, Al->Hf uses Hafnium column; absorber supplies only Delta_abs.
Hf tau_qp = 400 us adopted (caption/lit) over the 1 ms table cell, flagged MEDIUM.
Ta absorber gap encoded as bulk alpha-Ta BCS assumption 0.68 meV (MEDIUM), film phase flagged for Phase 5.

convention_lock.metric_signature: not_applicable — no relativistic field theory in this detector/rate pipeline
convention_lock.natural_units: internal-only (hbar=c=1) for CEvNS cross section; k_B EXPLICIT (not =1); I/O in eV/keV/MeV, counts/kg/day/keV, s, cm/um; (hbar c)^2 = 3.894e-28 GeV^2 cm^2
convention_lock.renormalization_scheme: tree-level SM (no loops); only scheme-dependent input is sin2thetaW = 0.2387 (low-energy MS-bar)
convention_lock.coordinate_system: Cartesian wafer frame: x,y in-plane 4in x 4in face, z through 2mm thickness; sensors on one z-face
convention_lock.coupling_convention: CEvNS dsigma/dT = (G_F^2 M/4pi) Q_W^2 (1 - M T/2 E_nu^2) F^2(q^2); prefactor /4pi NOT /8pi; Q_W = N-(1-4 sin2thetaW)Z; sin2thetaW=0.2387 (low-E MSbar); 1-4sin2thetaW=0.0452; Helm F, F(0)=1

custom_conventions.energy_scale_chain: single unified phonon scale, NO ionization quenching, for BOTH NR (CEvNS) and ER (muon/Compton): T=E_nr -> E_ph -> E_dep -> E_rec; E_ph=E_dep-E_stored(defects) (few-% NR-only, 0 for muons/Compton); E_rec(low-E)~=0.5*E_dep; FORBIDDEN: keVee/keVnr mixing, Lindhard/ionization quenching
custom_conventions.detector_normalization: Ge 8.29e24 atoms/kg, rho=5.323 g/cm^3, M=72.63 g/mol; wafer 4inx4inx2mm=20.65 cm^3~=110 g, ~10300 sensors 1/mm^2 one face; reactor 3 GW_th (thermal) at 25 m => ~7-8e12 nubar/cm^2/s; adopt 110 g geometry but KEEP per-kg (counts/kg/day) normalization; '1 kg' framing in SUMMARY.md is STALE
custom_conventions.efficiency_mapping: eps~=0.5 deposited-to-signal, imposed forward-model definition, SAME baseline both designs with +/-10-20% design-dependent band; Ta->Al and Al->Hf may split to per-design numbers in Phase 5; paper physical estimate eta_ce~=0.3 is an independent cross-reference, NOT baseline
custom_conventions.bandwidth_censoring: LOCKED resolving time: 25 kHz max resolvable tunneling rate => 40 us (Nyquist from 50 kHz bw); 20 us at 50 kHz sampling itself (state both); paralyzable-vs-non-paralyzable AND merge-vs-drop kept as EXPLICIT CODE SWITCH (not fixed); OPEN QUESTION BLOCKS Phase 5; both variants must be implementable
custom_conventions.cevns_benchmark_target: Phase-3 unit test: FULL Q_W => sigma(Ge,4 MeV)~=1.0e-40 cm^2 (canonical); N-only quick-check ~1.1e-40 cm^2 (1.08e-40, ~20% tol); coefficient sigma~=4.22e-45 N^2 (E_nu/MeV)^2 cm^2; closed form sigma_tot=G_F^2 Q_W^2 E_nu^2/4pi; PITFALLS.md ~1e-42 value is WRONG (100x)
